name: Data Preprocessing and Normalization

# Data Preprocessing and Normalization

Also called: Volume Preprocessing, Data Normalization

## Overview
Data Preprocessing and Normalization prepares volumetric data for [compression](#4-compression.md) and rendering by standardizing intensity distributions, correcting structural metadata, and restricting density ranges to improve compression ratios [S1, unofficial]. It differs from sibling methods like [Sparse structures](5-sparse-structures.md) or [Arithmetic Encoding](2127-arithmetic-encoding.md) by operating on the raw data values and geometry before any entropy coding or spatial subdivision occurs.

## Shared principles
Not given in the sources.

## Subtopics

### [Volume Normalization](1823-volume-normalization.md)
Scales a volume tensor to $[0, 1]$ while preserving constant positive masks as full foreground ($1.0$).

### [Volume Utility Functions](2677-volume-utility-functions.md)
Provides low-level operations for structural adjustments (dimensionality, voxel scale), format conversions (half-precision, normal encoding), and data integrity checks.

### [Dataset Preprocessing (DeepLesion)](7228-dataset-preprocessing-deeplesion.md)
Applies a specific, fixed thresholding and [cropping](#1648-cropping.md) pipeline tailored to the wide dynamic range of CT data, converting raw pixel intensities to Hounsfield Units (HU) and segmenting the body from background air.

### Density Range Restriction and Ramp Function
- **Definition**: A preprocessing function applied to volume data to restrict the range of density values, improving compression ratio by removing irrelevant data and avoiding discontinuities that generate high frequencies [S1, unofficial].
- **Step**: Apply function $T$ to each density value: if density $\le d_1$, set density $= 0$; if density $\ge d_4$, set density $= 0$; if $d_1 \le \text{density} \le d_2$, set density $= (\text{density} - d_1) \times d_2 / (d_2 - d_1)$; if $d_3 \le \text{density} \le d_4$, set density $= (d_3 - \text{density}) \times d_4 / (d_4 - d_3)$ [S1, unofficial]. Normalize models with histograms outside the $[0, 255]$ range to achieve the same output value range after applying $T$ [S1, unofficial].
- **Parameter**: $d_1, d_2, d_3, d_4$: Threshold parameters defining the density range $[d_2, d_3]$ to keep intact and the ramps $[d_1, d_2]$ and $[d_3, d_4]$ to avoid discontinuities [S1, unofficial].

## Background
The concept of restricting density ranges to improve compression is described in the context of volumetric medical images visualization on mobile devices, where a function $T$ is used to filter density values before compression [S1, unofficial]. General [volume normalization](#1823-volume-normalization.md) and utility functions are commonly found in deep learning and medical imaging pipelines (e.g., DeepLesion [dataset preprocessing](#7228-dataset-preprocessing-deeplesion.md)) to standardize inputs for generative models or rendering engines [S1, unofficial].
